docs.title: Agnostos
docs.text:
Resume-driven outreach for research internships. Agnostos is a free, open-source command-line tool that helps students find research internships:

  • Who should I write to? It ranks a professor list against your resume locally, for free, or builds the list for you from a research topic using the OpenAlex paper index.
  • What have they worked on lately? It pulls each professor's recent first- and last-author papers.
  • What do I say? One language-model call per professor returns an acceptance estimate and a short, specific, honest draft. Common AI tells are stripped out and unverifiable claims are flagged.
  • Is the address right? It checks every address and can find the one each professor publishes on their own page.
  • When do I send it? Slowly, from your own inbox, during each professor's working hours.
  • Did they answer? It tracks replies, auto-replies and bounces, and drafts follow-ups for you to approve.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Source on GitHub Technical report (PDF)

git clone https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Agnostos-v2
cd Agnostos-v2
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env                       # Windows: copy .env.example .env
python -m outreach.cli profile             # check resume parsing
python -m outreach.cli run --mode list     # score + draft into your xlsx
python -m outreach.cli send --dry-run      # preview the emails

The full command reference is in the README.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Setup: Windows · macOS · Linux Step-by-step installation and daily use for each operating system FAQ Common questions about costs, sending, replies and safety Diagnostics Health checks and fixes for every common error message Google Calendar One-time setup for meeting-slot checks and calendar holds Technical report (PDF) Architecture and every scoring rule: matcher, discovery ranking, cost estimate, AI-tell score, address confidence, scheduling

Note

Agnostos drafts; you decide. Nothing is sent without --live, and every draft is written to your spreadsheet first so you can read and edit it. The acceptance percentage is a model's estimate for ordering your list, not a statistical probability.

docs.title: Google Calendar setup
docs.text:
Agnostos uses Google Calendar for two things when it sends meeting requests (see Funding follow-ups and meeting requests):

  • Choosing slots. It never proposes a time when you're already busy.
  • Holding slots. When a reply goes out, each proposed time is added to your calendar as a tentative HOLD: call with <professor> event.

The setup is optional. Without it, meeting requests still go out; only the busy check and the holds are skipped.

It takes about 5 minutes and is done once.

docs.title: 1. Use the right Google account
docs.text:
Do every step while signed in to the personal Gmail whose calendar you want the holds on. Check the avatar in the top-right of the Cloud Console.

Most common failure: Error 403: org_internal. "Access blocked: <app> can only be used within its organization" means the Cloud project belongs to a Google Workspace organisation (a university or company account, or an org you created) and the app's audience is Internal. A personal Gmail can't sign in to an Internal app. Fix it in step 4 by making it External, or create the project with Location: No organization.

docs.title: 2. Create a project
docs.text:
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate.
  2. Give it any name, e.g. agnostos.
  3. Set Location / Organization to No organization if you can.
  4. Click Create, then make sure the new project is selected in the top bar.

docs.title: 3. Enable the Calendar API
docs.text: Open https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/calendar-json.googleapis.com and click Enable.

docs.title: 4. Configure the consent screen (Google Auth Platform)
docs.text:
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview and click Get started.
  2. App name: anything (e.g. Agnostos). Support email: your Gmail.
  3. Audience: choose External.
  4. Contact information: your Gmail. Accept the policy and click Create.
  5. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/audience:
  6. User type must read External. If it says Internal, click Make external and choose Testing, then Confirm.
  7. Under Test users, click Add users, add the Gmail you'll sign in with, then Save.

"Testing" needs no review by Google. Only the test users you list can sign in, which is exactly what you want.

docs.title: 5. Create a Desktop OAuth client
docs.text:
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients and click Create client.
  2. Application type: Desktop app. Name: anything.
  3. Click Create, then Download JSON.
  4. Save the file as credentials.json in the repo root, next to README.md, replacing any old one. Or set GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=path\to\file.json in .env.

credentials.json and the token are git-ignored. Never commit them.

docs.title: 6. Sign in once
docs.text:
python -m outreach.cli calendar-auth

A browser opens:

  1. Pick your Gmail.
  2. You'll see "Google hasn't verified this app". Click Continue; it's your own app.
  3. Allow access to Google Calendar.

The terminal then prints Authorised. Calendar: <your email> (<timezone>). The token is saved to output/gcal_token.json and refreshes itself, so you won't be asked again.

docs.title: 7. Settings (.env)
docs.text: Key Default Meaning GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET credentials.json Path to the OAuth client JSON GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID primary Calendar to check and write holds to MEET_MINUTES 20 Call length MEET_LEAD_DAYS 2 Earliest slot is this many days out MEET_THEIR_HOURS 9-17 Professor's local hours a slot must fit in MEET_MY_HOURS 13-23 Your hours (in MEET_MY_TZ) a slot must fit in MEET_MY_TZ Asia/Kolkata Your timezone MEET_LINK — Optional fixed Meet/Zoom link to include

docs.title: Switching accounts
docs.text:
To put holds on a different Google account:

  1. Delete output/gcal_token.json.
  2. If the new account isn't a test user, add it in step 4. If it's in a different project, also replace credentials.json.
  3. Run python -m outreach.cli calendar-auth again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Error 403: org_internal App audience is Internal. Go to Audience, click Make external, choose Testing, and add yourself as a test user. Or use a project with No organization. Error 403: access_denied The account you picked isn't a test user. Add it under Test users. Google Calendar not authorised Run calendar-auth. The token is missing or was deleted. OAuth client file not found Save the downloaded JSON as credentials.json in the repo root, or set GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET. invalid_grant on a later run The token was revoked or expired (Testing-mode tokens can expire after 7 days). Delete output/gcal_token.json and run calendar-auth again. Holds land on the wrong calendar You signed in with another account. See Switching accounts.

docs.title: Building the Agnostos desktop app
docs.text: Agnostos ships as a native Windows desktop app: a Tauri 2 shell (app/src-tauri, Rust), a React UI (app/src) and the Python engine (desktop_engine), which is frozen into agnostos-engine.exe and bundled as a Tauri sidecar. Nothing is hosted, and the app does not run in a browser. The shell talks to the engine over stdin/stdout as described in engine-protocol.md.

docs.title: Prerequisites (Windows 10/11 x64)
docs.text:
Tool Notes Visual Studio Build Tools (C++ workload, Windows SDK) MSVC linker for Rust Rust (stable, MSVC) winget install Rustlang.Rustup, then rustup default stable-msvc Node.js 20+ and npm cd app; npm install (pulls @tauri-apps/cli) Python 3.11+ Engine. PyInstaller is used for release builds WebView2 runtime Already present on Windows 11. The installer downloads it if missing

The first tauri build downloads NSIS and WiX automatically into the Tauri cache.

docs.title: Dev workflow
docs.text:
In dev mode the shell runs the engine straight from source. The env var only needs to be set in the shell that launches Tauri:

cd app
$env:AGNOSTOS_ENGINE_CMD = "python -m desktop_engine"   # run with cwd = repo root
# optional: $env:AGNOSTOS_ENGINE_CWD = "C:\path\to\repo"  (default: the repo containing app/)
npm run tauri dev                                        # starts Vite on :1420 + the Rust shell
  • To test the shell without the real engine, use $env:AGNOSTOS_ENGINE_CMD = "python tests\fake_engine.py".
  • If AGNOSTOS_ENGINE_CMD is not set, the shell starts the bundled sidecar binaries/agnostos-engine-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe. For dev builds build.rs creates an empty placeholder there if it is missing, so the sidecar fails to start and calls reject with unavailable.
  • Engine stderr and shell diagnostics go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.agnostos.desktop\logs\engine.log. The file rotates at 2 MB and keeps engine.1..3.log.
  • Rust tests: cd app\src-tauri; cargo test. These cover the protocol parser and router, plus a round trip through tests\fake_engine.py.

docs.title: Release build
docs.text:
.\build-app.ps1                    # engine + Tauri release build with build-machine paths remapped

or step by step:

.\build-engine.ps1                 # PyInstaller -> app\src-tauri\binaries\agnostos-engine-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe
cd app
npm run tauri build                # runs `npm run build` (Vite -> app/dist), compiles Rust, bundles

A release build fails early if the sidecar exe is missing or is the empty dev placeholder.

Outputs, under app\src-tauri\target\release\bundle\:

File Notes nsis\Agnostos_<ver>_x64-setup.exe Per-user install (no admin needed). Recommended download msi\Agnostos_<ver>_x64_en-US.msi Per-machine MSI for managed or enterprise installs

Each bundle is about 11 MB plus the size of the engine. The app version comes from app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (version) and Cargo.toml. Keep both in sync with outreach/__init__.py (__version__, currently 2.3.0) when you release.

docs.title: Publishing a download
docs.text:
1. Package the installer with docs: Agnostos-<ver>-Windows-Setup.zip containing the setup .exe, packaging/windows/README.md, USAGE.md and LICENSE.
  2. Tag the release (git tag v<ver>; push the tag) and create a GitHub Release with the ZIP attached. The README's Download link points at releases/latest.

docs.title: macOS build
docs.text: Run ./build-mac.sh on a Mac with the Xcode Command Line Tools, Python 3.12+, Node 20+ and Rust. It freezes the engine for the host target triple (agnostos-engine-aarch64-apple-darwin or -x86_64-apple-darwin), copies it into app/src-tauri/binaries/, and runs tauri build. tauri.macos.conf.json switches the bundle targets to app and dmg. The output is bundle/dmg/Agnostos_<ver>_<arch>.dmg. It is unsigned: the first time, right-click the app and choose Open. On macOS the engine keeps data in ~/Library/Application Support/Agnostos and stores tokens in the login Keychain (service Agnostos). See packaging/macos/README.md.

docs.title: Code signing
docs.text: Builds are unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn ("Windows protected your PC"). To sign them, set bundle.windows.certificateThumbprint (with digestAlgorithm: "sha256" and a timestampUrl) in tauri.conf.json, or use bundle.windows.signCommand for Azure Trusted Signing or a cloud HSM. Sign agnostos-engine.exe before bundling, because Tauri only signs the main exe and the installers.

docs.title: Auto-update
docs.text: Auto-update is not enabled. To add it, use tauri-plugin-updater: generate a key pair with npx tauri signer generate, set bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true, and set plugins.updater.pubkey and endpoints (for example a latest.json on GitHub Releases). Then sign release builds with TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY. Until then, users update by running the new installer, which upgrades in place and keeps per-user data in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Agnostos.

docs.title: Agnostos diagnostics
docs.text:
Use this when something isn't working. Start with the quick check, then find your error message in the tables below.

Never paste your .env or passwords into an issue or chat. Redact API keys and SMTP_PASSWORD/IMAP_PASSWORD.

docs.title: 1. Quick health check (2 minutes)
docs.text:
Run these from the repo folder, with the virtual environment active:

python --version                         # must be 3.10+
python -m outreach.cli tls-check         # certificates + reachability of SMTP, IMAP, LLM, OpenAlex
python -m outreach.cli profile           # resume parsing
python -m outreach.cli models            # LLM key works, model list
python -m outreach.cli stats             # workbook funnel + "why so few were sent"
python -m outreach.cli send --dry-run --preview 1   # drafts load, nothing is sent
python -m outreach.cli check-replies --dry-run      # IMAP login + reply detection
Command Healthy output tls-check ok on every host, and a trust source of "OS trust store (truststore)" or a certifi path profile your name, email, interests and projects models a list of model IDs stats counts, plus a "Why so few were sent" list if anything is blocked send --dry-run dry-run lines, then failed=0 check-replies --dry-run Folders: INBOX, ..., then a summary

The first command that fails tells you which section below to read.

docs.title: 2. Certificates / TLS
docs.text:
Symptoms 

ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1144)
You may also see APIConnectionError: Connection error. from the LLM, or empty results from verify/discover.

Cause. Python can't find a CA store. This happens almost always with python.org Python on macOS, which ships without certificates. It also happens on Windows with some university chains, and behind antivirus or corporate proxies that inspect HTTPS.

Fix, in order: 1. pip install -U truststore certifi. Agnostos then uses the OS trust store (Keychain, Windows CertStore or /etc/ssl). 2. macOS python.org build: double-click /Applications/Python 3.x/Install Certificates.command. 3. Linux: sudo apt install --reinstall ca-certificates (or your distro's equivalent). 4. Behind a proxy or antivirus that inspects TLS, export its root CA and set: SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/root.pem (Windows: $env:SSL_CERT_FILE="C:\path\root.pem") 5. Re-run python -m outreach.cli tls-check.

Never "fix" this by turning verification off.

docs.title: 3. Sending (SMTP)
docs.text:
Error Meaning Fix SMTPAuthenticationError (535) Login rejected Use an app password (Gmail/iCloud), not your normal password. Check SMTP_USER is the full address SMTPSenderRefused From address not allowed SMTP_FROM must equal the mailbox in SMTP_USER SMTPServerDisconnected: Connection unexpectedly closed / read operation timed out The server dropped the session. University relays drop idle sessions after about 2 minutes Agnostos reconnects before each email and retries the connection 3 times. If it persists: raise SEND_DELAY_MIN, lower DAILY_SEND_CAP, and wait an hour, because you may be temporarily rate-limited SMTPConnectError / TimeoutError on connect Can't reach host:port Check SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_SECURITY (465 uses ssl, 587 uses starttls). Some networks and VPS providers block SMTP ports, so try another network SMTPRecipientsRefused Bad recipient address Run verify --repair --apply on that row SMTPDataError (550/554) Message rejected, often as spam Shorten the draft, remove links, send fewer per day ! Stopped: 3 consecutive SMTP failures Safety stop The rest stay unsent and safe. Fix the cause above and re-run skipped: invalid address verify marked it undeliverable verify --repair --apply, or --allow-unverified if you're sure held ... outside local window It's outside 9-17 for that professor Expected. Re-run later or add --wait is open in Excel (or otherwise locked) Workbook locked Close Excel. If a sidecar .pending-status.json exists, it is merged automatically

Is my account flagged? Check these signs: - Your own sent copies arrive in your inbox fine, but professors say they got nothing: you're probably landing in spam. - Many bounced rows in check-replies with "rejected" or "blocked" wording. - Login suddenly fails after many sends.

If you see these, stop for 24-48 hours, then resume at 20-30 per day.

Test SMTP without emailing anyone: 

python -m outreach.cli send --review --top 1     # sends one draft to YOU

docs.title: 4. Reading replies (IMAP)
docs.text: Error Fix IMAP failed: ... AUTHENTICATIONFAILED Set IMAP_USER/IMAP_PASSWORD, which default to the SMTP ones. Gmail needs IMAP enabled in settings and an app password IMAP failed: ... getaddrinfo failed IMAP_HOST is wrong. It defaults to imap.<smtp domain>, so set it explicitly Replies exist but aren't detected They may be in a folder that isn't scanned. Set IMAP_FOLDERS=INBOX;Spam;Junk;<folder> replies finds threads but no "student" messages Your server doesn't keep a Sent copy. That's fine, because the original email is taken from the workbook

docs.title: 5. Drafting (LLM)
docs.text: Error / symptom Fix ~ endpoint rejected structured outputs ... retrying without it Normal. The endpoint doesn't support that feature and Agnostos adapts response truncated; raise MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS Reasoning models (gpt-5, o-series) use hidden tokens. Agnostos now raises the budget automatically. For other models, set MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=3000 Three consecutive failures; aborting to avoid wasted spend Look at the LLM Status column for the real error, then re-run run AuthenticationError / 401 Wrong or expired API key NotFoundError / model not found Check DRAFT_MODEL against python -m outreach.cli models RateLimitError / 429 Groq free tier limit. Wait a minute, lower --max-professors, or switch provider Set DRAFT_MODEL in .env Add DRAFT_MODEL=... Drafts sound robotic Keep HUMANIZE_REWRITE=true and lower HUMANIZE_THRESHOLD

docs.title: 6. Finding professors and emails
docs.text: Symptom Fix OpenAlex rate limit hit Set OPENALEX_MAILTO=you@... (polite pool), or get a free OPENALEX_API_KEY Many invalid / no address on this row verify --repair --apply --workers 6. Some professors don't publish an address, and those are left blank on purpose discover finds too few Broaden --query topics, widen --countries, lower --min-h-index verify very slow Lower --workers if you get blocked, or raise it if your network is fast

docs.title: 7. Interruptions (sleep, crash, power cut)
docs.text:
Nothing that was sent is ever lost or re-sent.

  1. Check whether a send is still running:
  2. Windows: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='python.exe'" | ? CommandLine -match "send --live"
  3. macOS/Linux: pgrep -af "outreach.cli send"
  4. Check what happened: tail -n 40 output/daily_send.log (Windows: Get-Content output\daily_send.log -Tail 40)
  5. Check the counts: python -m outreach.cli stats
  6. If nothing is running and rows are still unsent, re-run the same send --live ... command. It continues from where it stopped.

Windows sleep and wake history: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; ProviderName='Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Power','Microsoft-Windows-Power-Troubleshooter'} -MaxEvents 20 macOS: pmset -g log | grep -E "Sleep|Wake" | tail -20 · Linux: journalctl -b -u systemd-suspend

docs.title: 8. Workbook problems
docs.text: Symptom Fix PermissionError / is open in Excel Close Excel or LibreOffice Columns not recognised Headers must include a name column and an email column. See README "header mapping" Something got overwritten Restore from output/professors.backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.xlsx Statuses "missing" after a run Look for professors.xlsx.pending-status.json. It is merged on the next run, or run stats (which already counts it)

docs.title: 9. Reporting a bug
docs.text:
Include: 1. Your OS and python --version 2. The exact command you ran 3. The full error output, with emails, keys and passwords redacted 4. The output of python -m outreach.cli tls-check and python -m outreach.cli stats 5. The last 40 lines of output/daily_send.log, if it was a scheduled send

Open an issue at https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Agnostos-v2/issues.

docs.title: Agnostos desktop: engine protocol (v1)
docs.text:
The desktop app has three parts:

app/                Tauri 2 shell (Rust, app/src-tauri) + React/TypeScript UI (app/src)
desktop_engine/     Python engine, frozen with PyInstaller as `agnostos-engine.exe`
outreach/           existing CLI pipeline, called by the engine (unchanged behaviour)

Tauri starts agnostos-engine.exe as a sidecar and talks to it over stdin/stdout using newline-delimited JSON (UTF-8, one object per line). stderr is for diagnostics only. Nothing listens on a network port, except the short-lived 127.0.0.1 loopback redirect during Google sign-in.

docs.title: Tauri bridge (frontend ↔ Rust)
docs.text:
• invoke("engine_call", { method, params }) → resolves with result, or rejects with { code, message } (the engine error object; Rust uses code unavailable if the engine process is not running).
  • listen("engine://event", e => e.payload) where payload is { event, data }.
  • invoke("engine_restart") restarts the sidecar.
  • File pickers: @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog open({filters:[{name:"Resume",extensions:["pdf","docx"]}]}).
  • External links / OAuth browser: the engine opens the browser itself; the UI may use @tauri-apps/plugin-opener openUrl() for GitHub's verification URI.
  • In plain browser dev (npm run dev without Tauri) src/lib/engine.ts falls back to an in-memory mock implementing the same methods, so screens can be built and tested without Rust or Python.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Request (UI → engine, forwarded by Rust): 

{"id": 7, "method": "settings.get", "params": {}}
Response: 
{"id": 7, "result": {...}}
{"id": 7, "error": {"code": "not_signed_in", "message": "Sign in first"}}
Event (engine → UI, no id). Rust re-emits these as Tauri event engine://event: 
{"event": "job.log", "data": {"job_id": "j3", "line": "  [4/40] sent ..."}}

Error codes: bad_request, not_signed_in, not_found, conflict, confirmation_required, auth_failed, unavailable, internal.

Long operations (OAuth, resume parse, test connections) may take seconds; the UI must show progress. Pipeline work runs as jobs (see below) and returns immediately with a job_id.

docs.title: Types (TypeScript)
docs.text:
type User = { id: string; name: string; email: string | null;
              provider: "guest" | "local" | "google" | "github";
              avatar_url?: string | null; gmail_connected: boolean };

type OnboardingStep = "resume" | "profile" | "interests" | "targets" |
                      "email" | "llm" | "funding" | "limits";
type Onboarding = { completed: OnboardingStep[]; done: boolean };

type Profile = { name: string; email: string; degree: string; institution: string;
                 research_interests: string[]; skills: string[];
                 projects: { title: string; summary: string }[];
                 resume_file: string | null };

type Settings = Record<string, string>;     // .env-style keys; secrets come back masked "••••abcd"

type CommandField = { name: string; type: "bool" | "int" | "float" | "str" | "choice";
                      label: string; help?: string; default?: unknown;
                      choices?: string[]; min?: number; max?: number };
type CommandSpec = { name: string; title: string; group: string; description: string;
                     fields: CommandField[]; live_field?: string;   // field that makes it send real mail
                     confirmation?: string };                       // text user must type when live

type Job = { id: string; command: string; options: Record<string, unknown>;
             status: "running" | "waiting_input" | "done" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "interrupted";
             started: string; finished?: string | null; exit_code?: number | null;
             live: boolean; prompt?: string | null };

type Stats = { total: number; with_email: number; drafted: number; sent: number;
               replied: number; bounced: number; resends: number;
               sent_per_day: { date: string; count: number }[] };

type Professor = { row: number; sheet: string; name: string; email: string;
                   institution: string; country: string; probability: number;
                   send_status: string; reply_status: string; subject: string;
                   draft: string; version: string };            // version = optimistic-lock token

type ReplyDraft = { index: number; name: string; email: string; subject: string;
                    their_message: string; summary: string; action: string;
                    body: string; approved: boolean; sent_at: string | null };

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Params Result app.info – {version, engine_version, data_dir, user: User\|null, onboarding: Onboarding} auth.status – {user: User\|null} auth.guest {name?} {user} auth.register {name, email, password} {user} (local account, PBKDF2-hashed) auth.login {email, password} {user} auth.google {connect_gmail: bool} {user} — opens system browser, loopback redirect, PKCE. With connect_gmail, also stores a refresh token for Gmail SMTP/IMAP (XOAUTH2) auth.github.start – {user_code, verification_uri, device_code, interval, expires_in} (device flow) auth.github.poll {device_code} {status: "pending"\|"slow_down"\|"done"\|"expired"\|"denied", user?} auth.logout – {ok} onboarding.get – Onboarding onboarding.complete {step} Onboarding resume.import {path} {profile: Profile} — copies file into the user's workspace and parses it profile.get / profile.update – / {profile} {profile} settings.get – {settings, secrets: string[]} settings.update {values} {settings} — masked values are ignored, empty string clears email.test {kind: "smtp"\|"imap"} {ok, detail} llm.test – {ok, detail, models?: string[]} stats.get – Stats professors.list {query?, status?, offset?, limit?} {items: Professor[], total} drafts.update {sheet, row, version, subject?, draft} {professor} — refuses sent rows / stale version (conflict) replies.list – {items: ReplyDraft[], version} replies.update {index, version, body, approved} {version} conversations.get – {html, modified} commands.list – {commands: CommandSpec[]} — every CLI command, safe fields only jobs.start {command, options, confirmation?} {job: Job} — live mail requires exact confirmation text jobs.list – {jobs: Job[]} jobs.log {job_id, offset?} {lines: string[], offset} jobs.answer {job_id, answer: "y"\|"n"} {ok} — answers the CLI's own [Y/N] prompt jobs.cancel {job_id} {ok} — refused for live jobs mid-delivery dialog.none – – (file pickers are done in Tauri, paths passed to resume.import)

Events: job.log {job_id, line}, job.status {job: Job}, job.prompt {job_id, text}, auth.progress {stage, detail}.

docs.title: Data layout
docs.text: Per-user data lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Agnostos\users\<user_id>\ with workspace\.env, workspace\output\, workspace\resume.*. Secrets in .env are written by the engine only; OAuth refresh tokens are DPAPI-encrypted in tokens.bin. A user can instead point the app at an existing v2 checkout (settings.update {"_workspace": "C:\\path"}), which keeps existing outreach data and scheduled CLI tasks working.

docs.title: OAuth configuration
docs.text:
Client IDs are not secrets for desktop apps but are not committed either; the engine reads %LOCALAPPDATA%\Agnostos\oauth.json: 

{"google": {"client_id": "...apps.googleusercontent.com", "client_secret": "..."},
 "github": {"client_id": "Iv1...."}}
If a provider is not configured, auth.google/auth.github.start return unavailable with setup instructions, and the UI hides or disables the button.

docs.title: UI notes (frontend agent)
docs.text:
No contract changes. Things the engine/shell should know so the UI behaves well:

  • Extra settings keys written via settings.update (plain .env keys; please persist/return them in settings.get even if the CLI ignores them for now): TARGET_UNIVERSITIES (;-separated), SEND_WEEKDAYS (mon,tue,...; default weekdays), plus the existing DISCOVER_COUNTRIES (comma ISO codes, or europe), GEOGRAPHY, POSITION, FOCUS_KEYWORDS (;-joined interests), CAN_SELF_FUND (true/false), SELF_FUND_NOTE, DAILY_SEND_CAP, SEND_DELAY_MIN/MAX, SEND_LOCAL_WINDOW (9-11 or empty), LLM_PROVIDER, GROQ_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY, DRAFT_MODEL, SMTP_*, IMAP_*. _workspace is shown/edited in Settings → Workspace, so settings.get should include it.
  • email.test / llm.test are called right after settings.update, so they must read fresh values.
  • professors.list status values the UI sends: "" (all), unsent, sent, replied, failed (failed sends + bounces). Sent rows are detected client-side as send_status in sent/review-sent.
  • jobs.log is called with offset: 0 when a job is opened; live lines then come from job.log events. job.status events should carry the full Job (incl. prompt when waiting_input).
  • A CommandSpec with live_field renders that field inside a red "Danger zone"; when on, the UI requires typing confirmation exactly (falls back to SEND if missing) and passes it to jobs.start. Other fields are rendered by type; default, min, max, choices, help are honoured.
  • conversations.get.html is rendered in <iframe sandbox="" srcdoc> (no scripts, no same-origin).
  • auth.progress detail is shown under the Google button while auth.google is pending.
  • Shell (Tauri capabilities): the UI uses core:event listen (engine://event), dialog:allow-open, opener:allow-open-url (github.com/login/device, console.groq.com, platform.openai.com), and getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent for native resume drops (keep dragDropEnabled on). Vite dev server: http://localhost:1420, build output app/dist.

docs.title: Agnostos FAQ
docs.text: These are common questions about using Agnostos (v2, the command-line tool). For setup, see the guide for your OS: Windows · macOS · Linux. If something is broken, go to Diagnostics.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
What does Agnostos actually do? It reads your resume and finds professors whose recent papers overlap with your work (or uses a list you give it). It checks their email addresses and drafts one short, honest email per professor. It sends them slowly from your own mailbox, during each professor's working hours. It then watches your inbox for replies and drafts follow-ups for you to approve.

Does it send from my email address? Yes. Mail goes out through your own SMTP account, so replies come back to your normal inbox. Nothing passes through a third-party mail service.

Is it free? The tool is free and open source. The only cost is the language model: - Groq has a free tier that covers normal use. - OpenAI gpt-5-mini costs roughly $0.004 per drafted email, so 300 drafts cost about $1.20.

Before any paid call, run shows a cost estimate and asks Y/N. BUDGET_USD sets a hard limit.

What data leaves my computer? - To the model provider: your resume summary and each professor's public info (name, institution, recent paper titles). - To OpenAlex and university websites: lookups of public academic data. - To your mail server: the emails themselves.

Your .env, workbook and logs stay local. .env is git-ignored, so never commit it.

docs.title: Drafting
docs.text:
Will it make up achievements or results? It is instructed not to. Drafts describe what you built and tried, never metrics, "improvements" or novelty claims. A cleanup pass removes common AI-sounding phrases, and drafts that still read as machine-written get rewritten. Always read a few drafts yourself with send --review --top 3 before sending for real.

Why were only some professors drafted? Run python -m outreach.cli stats. Its "Why rows were / weren't drafted" section gives the reason for each row: - skipped: no email means there is no address. Try verify --repair --apply. - skipped: local score ... < 0.25 means the topic overlap is weak. Lower it with run --min-score 0.15. - skipped: over max-professors cap means the cap was hit. Raise it with run --max-professors 400. - skipped: budget exhausted means BUDGET_USD was reached. - failed: ... means a model error. See Diagnostics.

Can I edit a draft before it's sent? Yes. Open the workbook and edit the Custom Email Draft or Email Subject cell, then save and close it. The sender uses whatever is in the cell.

Can I re-draft everything with a different model? run --model gpt-4.1 --max-professors N redrafts. Rows already marked sent keep their status and are never mailed again.

What's the "Probability of Acceptance"? It is the model's calibrated guess (1-100) at how likely this professor is to take you. It's useful for ordering who to email first (send --top 20), not as a prediction.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
Why does it send so slowly? On purpose. University and Gmail servers throttle or flag accounts that send many near-identical emails quickly. The defaults are 40 per day, 5-10 minutes apart, and only 9:00-17:00 on weekdays in the professor's own time zone. This keeps your account healthy and makes it more likely your email is read.

Can I send more per day? You can raise DAILY_SEND_CAP, but more than about 50 per day from one personal mailbox risks rate limits or spam flags. A better approach is to schedule a daily run (see your OS guide) and let it finish over a week or two.

Will anyone get emailed twice? No: - A row marked sent is skipped on every later run unless you pass --resend. - Each successful send is written to the workbook immediately, so a crash, sleep or power cut can't lose that record. - If the workbook is open in Excel, statuses are saved to <workbook>.pending-status.json and merged on the next run.

What do --local-window 9-17 --wait do? --local-window 9-17 only sends while it's 9:00-17:00 on a weekday at the professor's location (taken from the Country column). Without --wait, rows outside that window are "held" for a later run. With --wait, the process stays running and sends each row when its window opens.

What's the difference between --dry-run, --review and --live? | Flag | Who receives it | Marks rows sent? | |---|---|---| | --dry-run (default) | nobody, it only prints | no | | --review | you (subject starts [DRAFT -> prof@...]) | no (marked review-sent, doesn't block the real send) | | --live | the professors | yes | | --export | writes .eml files to output/drafts/ | no |

Is my CV attached? Only if you set ATTACHMENTS=/path/to/cv.pdf in .env. Separate multiple files with ;. Follow-up replies are sent without attachments.

Why was an address skipped as "invalid"? verify found it undeliverable, for example a nonexistent domain or a format the university doesn't use. Run verify --repair --apply to find the right one. Use --allow-unverified only if you are sure the address is correct.

Can I stop a send halfway? Yes. Press Ctrl+C, or close the window. Everything sent so far is already recorded, and the next run continues where it stopped.

docs.title: Replies
docs.text:
How does it know who replied? check-replies logs into your mailbox over IMAP (read-only). It matches messages by the professor's address and by the original Message-ID, then sorts each one into replied, auto-reply (out-of-office) or bounced. It writes the result to the Reply Status column. It checks INBOX and any spam/junk folders.

How are follow-ups drafted? replies reads the whole thread for each professor, both your sent messages and theirs. For every thread where the professor wrote last, it chooses one of: - reply: they asked something or left a door open, so it answers their questions. - thank: a polite no. It drafts a short thank-you, often asking whether they know a colleague who takes students. - none: nothing worth sending.

Drafts are saved to output/reply_queue.json. Nothing is sent until you set "approved": true and run replies --send --live.

Will follow-ups show up in the same thread? Yes. They're sent with Re: in the subject and with In-Reply-To/References headers, so mail clients group them with the original conversation.

It wrote [FILL: ...] in a reply. Why? The professor asked for something the model doesn't know, such as your GPA, exact dates or a transcript link. Replace the placeholder before approving.

docs.title: Running unattended
docs.text:
Can I leave it running overnight or close my laptop? Closing the lid usually sleeps the machine and pauses sending. Nothing is lost, and it resumes when the machine wakes. To keep it sending: - Windows: turn off the lid-close sleep action on AC power, or use PowerToys Awake. - macOS: caffeinate -i (already in the launchd example), or clamshell mode. - Linux: systemd-inhibit (already in the systemd example).

How do I check progress from my phone? Install Tailscale on both devices, SSH into the computer, and run python -m outreach.cli stats or tail -f output/daily_send.log. Your OS guide has the details.

Where are the logs? | File | Contents | |---|---| | output/professors.xlsx | Everything: drafts, statuses, sent times, replies | | output/send_log.csv | One line per send attempt (dry-run, review, live), kept even if the sheet is edited | | output/daily_send.log | Console output of scheduled sends | | output/reply_queue.json | Drafted follow-ups awaiting approval | | output/professors.backup-*.xlsx | Automatic backups taken before each run |

docs.title: Accounts and providers
docs.text:
Which email providers work? Anything with SMTP and IMAP: | Provider | SMTP | IMAP | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Gmail / Google Workspace | smtp.gmail.com 465 ssl | imap.gmail.com 993 | Needs 2FA and an app password | | Outlook / Microsoft 365 | smtp.office365.com 587 starttls | outlook.office365.com 993 | Many orgs disable SMTP AUTH, so ask IT | | iCloud | smtp.mail.me.com 587 starttls | imap.mail.me.com 993 | App-specific password | | Most universities | smtp.<uni> 465 ssl or 587 starttls | imap.<uni> 993 | Check your IT pages |

Is sending from my university address better than Gmail? Usually yes. Professors are more likely to open it, and university mail is less likely to land in spam. Universities also rate-limit more strictly, so keep the default pacing.

Can I use a different model provider? Yes, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. Set LLM_PROVIDER=openai, OPENAI_BASE_URL=<url>, OPENAI_API_KEY=<key> and DRAFT_MODEL=<model>. Agnostos detects at runtime which request features the endpoint supports.

docs.title: Agnostos on Linux
docs.text:
See also: FAQ · Diagnostics

This guide covers setup and daily use on Ubuntu/Debian, Fedora and Arch, as a desktop or a headless server. It runs Agnostos as a local command-line tool.

docs.title: 1. Install the prerequisites
docs.text:
# Ubuntu / Debian
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv python3-pip git ca-certificates

# Fedora
sudo dnf install -y python3 python3-pip git ca-certificates

# Arch
sudo pacman -S --needed python python-pip git ca-certificates

Python 3.10 or newer is required. Check with python3 --version.

docs.title: 2. Get the code
docs.text:
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Agnostos-v2.git
cd Agnostos-v2

docs.title: 3. Create a virtual environment and install
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -U pip
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 4. Configure .env
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env        # it holds passwords
nano .env

RESUME_PATH=/home/<you>/CV.pdf
TARGET_XLSX=/home/<you>/Agnostos-v2/output/professors.xlsx
ATTACHMENTS=/home/<you>/research_CV.pdf

LLM_PROVIDER=groq
GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...
# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
# DRAFT_MODEL=gpt-5-mini

SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
SMTP_PORT=465
SMTP_SECURITY=ssl
SMTP_USER=you@gmail.com
SMTP_PASSWORD=<app password>
SMTP_FROM=you@gmail.com

DAILY_SEND_CAP=40
SEND_DELAY_MIN=300
SEND_DELAY_MAX=600
SEND_LOCAL_WINDOW=9-17

Many cloud VPS providers block outbound port 25, and some block 465 and 587 on new accounts. Run python -m outreach.cli tls-check to confirm SMTP is reachable.

docs.title: 5. Check the setup
docs.text:
python -m outreach.cli profile
python -m outreach.cli models
python -m outreach.cli tls-check

docs.title: 6. The workflow
docs.text:
Step Command Find professors python -m outreach.cli discover --count 300 --batches 3 --verify-emails Fix emails python -m outreach.cli verify --repair --apply Score and draft python -m outreach.cli run --mode list --max-professors 300 Preview (sends nothing) python -m outreach.cli send --dry-run Review copies to yourself python -m outreach.cli send --review --top 3 Send for real, paced python -m outreach.cli send --live --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait Progress python -m outreach.cli stats Detect replies and bounces python -m outreach.cli check-replies Draft follow-ups python -m outreach.cli replies Send approved follow-ups python -m outreach.cli replies --send --live

The workbook is an .xlsx. You can open it in LibreOffice Calc, but close it before a live send. Already-sent rows are never re-sent unless you pass --resend.

docs.title: Option A: systemd user timer (recommended)
docs.text:
~/.config/systemd/user/agnostos-send.service 

[Unit]
Description=Agnostos paced outreach send

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=%h/Agnostos-v2
Environment=PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8
ExecStart=/usr/bin/systemd-inhibit --what=sleep:idle --why="Agnostos sending" \
  %h/Agnostos-v2/.venv/bin/python -u -m outreach.cli send --live --yes --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait
StandardOutput=append:%h/Agnostos-v2/output/daily_send.log
StandardError=append:%h/Agnostos-v2/output/daily_send.log

~/.config/systemd/user/agnostos-send.timer 

[Unit]
Description=Run Agnostos send on weekdays

[Timer]
OnCalendar=Mon..Fri 12:30
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target


systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now agnostos-send.timer
sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER          # keep running after you log out (servers)
systemctl --user list-timers | grep agnostos
systemctl --user start agnostos-send        # run now
journalctl --user -u agnostos-send -f       # or: tail -f output/daily_send.log

systemd-inhibit stops the machine from sleeping while the send runs. Persistent=true catches up on a run that was missed while the machine was off.

docs.title: Option B: cron
docs.text:
crontab -e

30 12 * * 1-5 cd $HOME/Agnostos-v2 && PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 .venv/bin/python -u -m outreach.cli send --live --yes --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait >> output/daily_send.log 2>&1

Cron uses the system timezone. Check it with timedatectl.

docs.title: 8. Keep the machine awake (laptops)
docs.text:
• Use systemd-inhibit as in Option A, or prefix a manual run: systemd-inhibit --what=sleep:idle python -m outreach.cli send --live ...
  • To keep running with the lid closed on power, set HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=ignore in /etc/systemd/logind.conf, then run sudo systemctl restart systemd-logind.
  • On a headless server, run long manual jobs inside tmux so they survive SSH disconnects: tmux new -s agnostos â†’ run the command â†’ Ctrl+B D to detach â†’ tmux attach -t agnostos to return.

If the machine sleeps anyway, nothing is lost. Each sent email is saved immediately, and the waits use the wall clock.

docs.title: 9. Monitor remotely (optional)
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up --ssh            # Tailscale SSH, no sshd config needed
From another device: 
ssh <you>@<machine-name>
cd ~/Agnostos-v2 && source .venv/bin/activate
python -m outreach.cli stats
tail -f output/daily_send.log

docs.title: 10. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED sudo apt install --reinstall ca-certificates (or your distro's equivalent), then pip install -U truststore certifi and python -m outreach.cli tls-check. For a custom CA: export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/root.pem error: externally-managed-environment You're outside the venv. Run source .venv/bin/activate No module named venv sudo apt install python3-venv SMTPConnectError / timeout on a VPS Your provider blocks SMTP. Ask them to unblock it, or use a different port or host SMTPAuthenticationError Use an app password. Check SMTP_USER Timer didn't fire systemctl --user list-timers. On servers, make sure loginctl enable-linger was run Few emails sent python -m outreach.cli stats explains why rows were skipped

docs.title: Agnostos on macOS
docs.text:
See also: FAQ · Diagnostics

This guide covers setup and daily use on macOS 12 or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel. It runs Agnostos as a local command-line tool.

Prefer the desktop app? Build the .dmg once with ./build-mac.sh; see packaging/macos/README.md. The app offers the same commands, including the funding factor, company search and senior-researcher (legacy) letters.

docs.title: 1. Install the prerequisites
docs.text:
Use Homebrew (https://brew.sh):

brew install python@3.12 git
python3 --version

If you use the python.org installer instead: it ships without any SSL certificates. Every connection then fails with [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:...). Fix it once by double-clicking /Applications/Python 3.x/Install Certificates.command. Agnostos also installs truststore, so it reads the macOS Keychain directly. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 2. Get the code
docs.text:
cd ~/Desktop
git clone https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Agnostos-v2.git
cd Agnostos-v2

docs.title: 3. Create a virtual environment and install
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -U pip
pip install -r requirements.txt

Run source .venv/bin/activate in every new terminal before using python -m outreach.cli ....

docs.title: 4. Configure .env
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
open -e .env          # or: nano .env

Fill in section 1 at minimum. Use full macOS paths:

RESUME_PATH=/Users/<you>/Documents/CV.pdf
TARGET_XLSX=/Users/<you>/Desktop/Agnostos-v2/output/professors.xlsx
ATTACHMENTS=/Users/<you>/Documents/research_CV.pdf

LLM_PROVIDER=groq                # free; or openai
GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...
# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
# DRAFT_MODEL=gpt-5-mini

SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
SMTP_PORT=465
SMTP_SECURITY=ssl                # ssl on 465, starttls on 587
SMTP_USER=you@gmail.com
SMTP_PASSWORD=<16-char app password>
SMTP_FROM=you@gmail.com

DAILY_SEND_CAP=40
SEND_DELAY_MIN=300
SEND_DELAY_MAX=600
SEND_LOCAL_WINDOW=9-17

Gmail / iCloud: use an app password. For Gmail, create one at https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords. For iCloud, go to appleid.apple.com â†’ Sign-In and Security â†’ App-Specific Passwords. iCloud SMTP is smtp.mail.me.com on port 587 with starttls.

docs.title: 5. Check the setup
docs.text:
python -m outreach.cli profile
python -m outreach.cli models
python -m outreach.cli tls-check     # must show "ok" for every host

docs.title: 6. The workflow
docs.text:
Step Command Find professors python -m outreach.cli discover --count 300 --batches 3 --verify-emails Fix emails python -m outreach.cli verify --repair --apply Score and draft python -m outreach.cli run --mode list --max-professors 300 Preview (sends nothing) python -m outreach.cli send --dry-run Review copies to yourself python -m outreach.cli send --review --top 3 Send for real, paced python -m outreach.cli send --live --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait Progress python -m outreach.cli stats Detect replies and bounces python -m outreach.cli check-replies Draft follow-ups from full threads python -m outreach.cli replies Send approved follow-ups python -m outreach.cli replies --send --live

Close the workbook in Excel or Numbers before a live send. Already-sent rows are never mailed again unless you pass --resend.

docs.title: 7. Send automatically every weekday (launchd)
docs.text:
Create ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agnostos.send.plist. Replace <you> with your username:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>com.agnostos.send</string>
  <key>WorkingDirectory</key><string>/Users/<you>/Desktop/Agnostos-v2</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key><array>
    <string>/usr/bin/caffeinate</string><string>-i</string>
    <string>/Users/<you>/Desktop/Agnostos-v2/.venv/bin/python</string>
    <string>-u</string><string>-m</string><string>outreach.cli</string><string>send</string>
    <string>--live</string><string>--yes</string><string>--limit</string><string>40</string>
    <string>--local-window</string><string>9-17</string><string>--wait</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key><dict><key>PYTHONIOENCODING</key><string>utf-8</string></dict>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key><array>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>1</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>12</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>2</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>12</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>3</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>12</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>4</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>12</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>5</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>12</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer></dict>
  </array>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/<you>/Desktop/Agnostos-v2/output/daily_send.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/<you>/Desktop/Agnostos-v2/output/daily_send.log</string>
</dict></plist>

Load it and manage it: 

launchctl load  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agnostos.send.plist
launchctl start com.agnostos.send                     # run now
tail -f output/daily_send.log                         # live log
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agnostos.send.plist   # stop

The caffeinate -i wrapper keeps the Mac from idle-sleeping while a send is running.

If you keep the repo in ~/Desktop or ~/Documents, open System Settings â†’ Privacy & Security â†’ Full Disk Access and add /usr/bin/caffeinate and the venv's python. Without this, launchd can be blocked from reading those folders.

docs.title: 8. Keep the Mac awake
docs.text:
• During a manual run, start the command with caffeinate -i: caffeinate -i python -m outreach.cli send --live --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait
  • Closing the lid sleeps the Mac anyway unless it is on power with an external display attached (clamshell mode). Alternatively, run sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1 and undo it later with sudo pmset -a disablesleep 0.

If the Mac sleeps mid-run, nothing is lost. Each sent email is saved immediately, and the wait timers use the wall clock, so they resume correctly after wake.

docs.title: 9. Monitor remotely (optional)
docs.text:
Turn on System Settings â†’ General â†’ Sharing â†’ Remote Login. Install Tailscale, then connect from another device: 

ssh <you>@<tailscale-ip>
cd ~/Desktop/Agnostos-v2 && source .venv/bin/activate
python -m outreach.cli stats
tail -f output/daily_send.log

docs.title: 10. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED ... (_ssl.c:1144) or similar 1) pip install -U truststore certifi 2) run Install Certificates.command (python.org builds) 3) python -m outreach.cli tls-check. Behind a corporate proxy, export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/root.pem SMTPAuthenticationError Use an app password. Check SMTP_USER SMTPServerDisconnected Reconnects automatically. If it persists, raise SEND_DELAY_MIN and lower DAILY_SEND_CAP xcrun: error during pip install xcode-select --install zsh: command not found: python Use python3, or activate the venv launchd job never runs Check Full Disk Access (see section 7), then launchctl list \| grep agnostos Few emails sent python -m outreach.cli stats explains why rows were skipped

docs.title: Agnostos on Windows
docs.text:
See also: FAQ · Diagnostics

This guide covers setup and daily use on Windows 10 or 11. It runs Agnostos as a local command-line tool.

Just want the app? Download Agnostos-<version>-Windows-Setup.zip from the latest release, extract it, and run the setup .exe. You don't need Python, Node or Rust.

docs.title: 1. Install the prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Python 3.10 or newer, including Python 3.15. Get a stable release from https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/ and tick "Add python.exe to PATH" in the installer. Check it worked: 
    python --version
  2. Git. Get it from https://git-scm.com/download/win.

docs.title: 2. Get the code
docs.text:
cd $HOME\Desktop
git clone https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Agnostos-v2.git
cd Agnostos-v2

docs.title: 3. Create a virtual environment and install
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -U pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

The standard dependencies have Windows Python 3.15 wheels, so Visual C++ Build Tools are not required. If pip tries to compile PyYAML, run git pull first: older versions of Agnostos required PyYAML, which does not provide a Windows 3.15 wheel. After updating, create a fresh virtual environment as shown above and reinstall requirements. Use the same python or .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe for installation and CLI commands.

If PowerShell says running scripts is disabled, run this once and then activate again: 

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned

Activate the venv (.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1) in every new terminal before you run any python -m outreach.cli ... command.

docs.title: 4. Configure .env
docs.text:
Copy-Item .env.example .env
notepad .env

Fill in section 1 at minimum. Use full Windows paths:

RESUME_PATH=C:\Users\<you>\Documents\CV.pdf
TARGET_XLSX=C:\Users\<you>\Desktop\Agnostos-v2\output\professors.xlsx
ATTACHMENTS=C:\Users\<you>\Documents\research_CV.pdf

LLM_PROVIDER=groq                # free; or openai
GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...
# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...          # if LLM_PROVIDER=openai
# DRAFT_MODEL=gpt-5-mini

SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com         # university: e.g. smtp.iitd.ac.in
SMTP_PORT=465
SMTP_SECURITY=ssl                # ssl on 465, starttls on 587
SMTP_USER=you@gmail.com
SMTP_PASSWORD=<16-char app password>
SMTP_FROM=you@gmail.com

Gmail: turn on 2-Step Verification, then create an app password at https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords. Your normal password will not work.

Recommended pacing, so your mailbox doesn't get throttled: 

DAILY_SEND_CAP=40
SEND_DELAY_MIN=300
SEND_DELAY_MAX=600
SEND_LOCAL_WINDOW=9-17

docs.title: 5. Check the setup
docs.text:
python -m outreach.cli profile       # what was read from your resume
python -m outreach.cli models        # which models your key can use
python -m outreach.cli tls-check     # SMTP / IMAP / API certificates

docs.title: 6. The workflow
docs.text:
Step Command What it does Find professors python -m outreach.cli discover --count 300 --batches 3 --verify-emails Searches OpenAlex for active researchers in your topics and writes them to output\professors.xlsx Fix emails python -m outreach.cli verify --repair --apply Checks every address and replaces bad ones with the address on their university page Score and draft python -m outreach.cli run --mode list --max-professors 300 Scores each match and drafts one honest email per professor Preview python -m outreach.cli send --dry-run Prints the drafts. Nothing is sent Review in your inbox python -m outreach.cli send --review --top 3 Mails 3 drafts to yourself Send for real python -m outreach.cli send --live --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait Sends paced emails, only during each professor's local working hours Progress python -m outreach.cli stats Shows drafted, sent, replied and bounced counts, and why rows were skipped Replies python -m outreach.cli check-replies Marks replied, auto-reply and bounced rows in the workbook Draft follow-ups python -m outreach.cli replies Reads each full thread and drafts a reply into output\reply_queue.json Send follow-ups python -m outreach.cli replies --send --live Sends the queue items you set to "approved": true

Important rules: - Close the workbook in Excel before a live send. If it is open, statuses are saved to a sidecar file and merged on the next run. Nobody gets mailed twice. - Rows already marked sent are never sent again unless you pass --resend.

docs.title: 7. Send automatically every weekday (Task Scheduler)
docs.text:
This registers a task that sends up to 40 emails every weekday at 12:30. In IST, that covers the European morning.

$repo = "$HOME\Desktop\Agnostos-v2"
$py   = "$repo\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"
$cmd  = "cd /d `"$repo`" && set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 && `"$py`" -u -m outreach.cli send --live --yes --limit 40 --local-window 9-17 --wait >> output\daily_send.log 2>&1"
$action  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "cmd.exe" -Argument "/c $cmd"
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Monday,Tuesday,Wednesday,Thursday,Friday -At "12:30"
$set     = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew -ExecutionTimeLimit (New-TimeSpan -Hours 14) -WakeToRun -StartWhenAvailable -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Agnostos daily outreach send" -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $set -Force

Manage the task: 

Start-ScheduledTask   -TaskName "Agnostos daily outreach send"     # run now
Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName "Agnostos daily outreach send"     # last/next run
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Agnostos daily outreach send" -Confirm:$false
Get-Content output\daily_send.log -Tail 20 -Wait                   # live log

docs.title: 8. Keep the laptop awake
docs.text:
A paced send runs for hours, and closing the lid normally puts the laptop to sleep. Either:

  • Run these in an Administrator PowerShell to keep it running on charger with the lid closed: 
    powercfg /setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_BUTTONS LIDACTION 0
powercfg /setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_SLEEP STANDBYIDLE 0
powercfg /setactive SCHEME_CURRENT
  • Or install Microsoft PowerToys â†’ Awake and set it to "Keep awake indefinitely".

If the machine does sleep, nothing is lost. Each sent email is saved to the workbook immediately. The send continues after you wake the machine, or on the next scheduled run.

docs.title: 9. Monitor remotely (optional)
docs.text:
1. Install Tailscale on the PC and on your phone, and sign in on both.
  2. Enable the SSH server once, in an Administrator PowerShell: 
    Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0
Start-Service sshd; Set-Service sshd -StartupType Automatic
  3. From the phone or another computer, connect with ssh <windows-user>@<tailscale-ip> (find the IP with tailscale ip -4). Then run: 
    cd $HOME\Desktop\Agnostos-v2
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m outreach.cli stats
Get-Content output\daily_send.log -Tail 20 -Wait

docs.title: 10. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED pip install -U truststore certifi, then python -m outreach.cli tls-check. Behind antivirus or a proxy that inspects HTTPS, set SSL_CERT_FILE to its root certificate SMTPAuthenticationError Use an app password, not your login password. Check SMTP_USER SMTPServerDisconnected / read timed out The server drops idle sessions. Agnostos reconnects on its own. If it keeps happening, raise SEND_DELAY_MIN and lower DAILY_SEND_CAP SMTPSenderRefused SMTP_FROM must be the same mailbox as SMTP_USER response truncated from the LLM Fixed automatically for gpt-5 and o-series models. For other models, raise MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS Workbook "is open in Excel" Close Excel, then re-run Accented names print as ? $env:PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8" Few emails sent Run stats. It lists the reason, for example rows with no email, low match scores, the MAX_PROFESSORS cap, or the daily cap
